summary.document_title: SEV-1 Checkout Gateway Cascading Timeout Postmortem (INC-2026-884)
summary.executive_summary: Addresses the root causes of the 19-minute SEV-1 payment outage by introducing an adaptive circuit breaker with automatic failover to Acquirer-A and updating FIN-105 to enforce 4.5s timeouts with bulkhead connection isolation.
risks_and_dependencies: Automatic failover to Secondary Acquirer-A may increase per-transaction processing fees during brownouts.
Requires load-testing at 4,200+ req/s to validate bulkhead pool sizing (150 sockets).
open_questions: What is the maximum acceptable automatic failover fee differential when routing from Acquirer-B to Acquirer-A?
Should half-open circuit probe requests include high-value institutional wire transfers or only card authorizations under $500?

stories.title: Adaptive Acquirer Circuit Breaker with Automated Failover Routing
stories.user_story: As a Checkout Platform SRE, I want an adaptive circuit breaker that trips when upstream failure/timeout rates exceed 25% over 30s and routes traffic to Acquirer-A, so that single-acquirer latency spikes cannot cause cascading checkout outages.
stories.technical_description: Implement a state-machine circuit breaker (Closed -> Open -> Half-Open) around Acquirer-B client calls, configure automatic failover routing to Acquirer-A, and emit Prometheus state metrics + PagerDuty alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Given a 30-second rolling window with >= 25% timeout/5xx errors on Acquirer-B, when the threshold is breached, then the circuit trips OPEN within 500ms and routes subsequent requests to Acquirer-A.
Given an OPEN circuit for 60 seconds, when entering HALF-OPEN state, then probe requests validate upstream recovery before closing the circuit.
Prometheus exports `acquirer_circuit_state` gauge metrics and triggers a PagerDuty alert if OPEN duration exceeds 60 seconds.
stories.priority_rationale: Direct remediation for a customer-facing SEV-1 cascading payment outage.
stories.alignment_notes: Net-new resilience pattern complementing the timeout configuration in FIN-105.

stories.title: Enforce 4.5s Acquirer HTTP Timeout and 150-Socket Bulkhead Pool
stories.user_story: As a Backend Payment Engineer, I want upstream acquirer HTTP calls bounded to a 4.5-second timeout and isolated in a 150-connection bulkhead pool, so that slow upstream responses cannot exhaust global worker threads.
stories.technical_description: Update FIN-105 from a static 30s socket timeout to a 1.5s connect / 3.0s read timeout (4.5s total budget) and configure isolated connection pools capped at 150 concurrent sockets per acquirer.
acceptance_criteria: Given an upstream acquirer call exceeding 4.5 seconds total elapsed time, when the deadline expires, then the client aborts immediately and raises a typed AcquirerTimeoutError.
Given 150 concurrent in-flight requests to Acquirer-B, when request 151 arrives, then it fails fast via bulkhead rejection without starving Acquirer-A worker threads.
Load test at 4,200 req/s confirms zero global worker pool exhaustion when Acquirer-B latency is injected at 30 seconds.
stories.priority_rationale: Eliminates the thread-starvation vector that caused INC-2026-884.
stories.alignment_notes: Directly replaces the unsafe 30s timeout specification in existing backlog item FIN-105.
